First, Jackson is always bragging about how he was a 23-0 pro boxer, one of the best in the valley. But when I googled his name, nothing came up. That makes me think he's lying. I know I'm 19, have been training in Muay Thai for eight years, and I'm pretty fit. I used to be overweight too, so I've come a long way. I called him out on his boxing lies and challenged him to come to my gym. He got upset and left, and I told some coworkers about it. Most think I'm a asshole, but a few agree with me. So, is it right or wrong for me to call him out? Let me think about the pros and cons. On the positive side, I stood up for myself and called out someone who was lying. It's important to not let people take advantage of you or spread false information. Plus, I was confident in my own skills, which is good. Maybe I helped others see through his lies too. On the negative side, I confronted him in front of others, which could have been embarrassing. Maybe I should have talked to him privately instead of making a scene. Also, by telling other coworkers, I might have caused unnecessary drama or tension in the workplace. It's possible that some people saw me as the instigator, which is why most think I'm a asshole. I also need to consider the workplace dynamics. If Jackson is upset, it could affect our work relationship. Maybe I should have handled it more discreetly or through a manager. But I was angry in the moment, so I reacted without thinking. Another point is whether my challenge was appropriate. Challenging someone to a fight, even in a gym, can be seen as aggressive. It might have been better to just call him out on the lies without issuing a challenge. I also wonder about the impact on my reputation. By confronting him publicly, I might have made others see me as confrontational or mean, even if I was right. It's important to maintain a good relationship with coworkers, especially in a small workplace. In the end, while I think it's important to stand up against lies, the way I did it might have been too harsh. Maybe there's a better way to address the issue without causing conflict. But I also don't want to be seen as someone who lets people walk all over them. So, considering all this, I think it's a bit of both. It was right to call him out for lying, but the method and the aftermath might have been handled better. I should reflect on how to address such situations more effectively in the future.
